name: GTO Wizard
takeaway: Puts one button ('Begin Your Journey') and two named WSOP winners in the first screen, then splits the product into Analyze, Study and Practice cards.

name: Upswing Poker
takeaway: Leads with a named pro and course stats, follows with media logos and verified-customer quotes, and shows real prices ($7 and $999) on the home page.

name: PokerCoaching
takeaway: Puts a stats strip under the hero, repeats one button label ('Start Improving Today') three times, and ends on plan cards, an FAQ and a 30-day money-back guarantee.

name: Run It Once
takeaway: Uses 'Get Started For Free' as the single hero button and sells breadth with counts such as 186 pros, with no testimonials or prices on the page.

name: PokerTracker
takeaway: Its H1 is a release notice ('Now Available for Mac and Windows') followed by equal BUY NOW and DOWNLOAD buttons and a 14-day free trial, with no ratings or prices on the page.

name: Regroup Poker Tools
takeaway: A short store-badge page with four feature blocks each followed by 'Download Now', a closing 'get the app' band, and no ratings, logos or testimonials.

name: Nash Bankroll
takeaway: Opens with a plain promise ('Know your real poker results.') and one App Store button, then four feature blocks, an FAQ and a closing band, with no proof section.

name: Poker Analytics
takeaway: Puts a ratings bar (4.8 stars, 2,000+ ratings, tracking since 2012) under the buttons and gives import its own section, 'Switching trackers? Bring your history.'

name: Poker Bankroll Tracker
takeaway: A feature-list page with three download badges, a quote credited to Upswing, seven named players and a plain statement that data can be exported and imported as CSV.

name: Flighty
takeaway: Holds the first screen to one promise and an Apple Design Award line, puts 'Import your flights in seconds' right before its first 'Give Flighty a try' button, then closes on named reviews, a 3 million user count and a final button.

name: Copilot Money
takeaway: Puts an award and rating line between the subhead and the single 'Get started' button, and shows one plan with its price on the home page.

name: Aimchess
takeaway: Shows what is holding the player back, then personalized lessons, then a weekly study plan, backs it with one cited 31% research claim, and lists Free and paid prices on the page.

name: Strava
takeaway: Makes sign-up the hero with Google, Apple and email buttons, puts 'for free' and 100 million people in the subhead, and repeats 'Join Us Now' down the page.

name: Linear
takeaway: Lets a real product UI carry the hero, keeps the sign-up button in the header, and saves customer quotes and the 40,000-team count for just before the closing 'Get started' band.

name: Raycast
takeaway: Backs its pitch with 24 named user testimonials and concrete numbers such as a 99.8% crash-free rate, and closes with 'Download and use Raycast for free.'

name: Superhuman
takeaway: Pairs a quantified outcome ('Save 4+ hours each week') with a button that names the product ('Get Mail') and a customer logo strip right below, and two fetch methods returned different heroes.
